scope: In-process detachment/concurrency mechanism only, inside internal/pipeline and internal/shared/concurrency: Service.StartRun builds a detached+bounded run context via the existing RunContext helper, hands the run to a new shared/concurrency.Supervisor (no bare `go`), a new Orchestrator publishes lifecycle events to the existing Hub regardless of subscriber presence, and a MaxConcurrentRuns semaphore gates handoff. No frontend, no real LLM provider, no BYO-key resolution, no RAG retrieval, no memory integration, no context-warning gate, no database-backed pipeline persistence (Service stays in-memory, same as task 009 established), no Gin/HTTP/SSE routes or OpenAPI docs (that is task 012), and no change to the 7-stage sequence itself (transition.go/Order untouched). cmd/gateway/main.go is deliberately NOT wired to construct Service/Supervisor in this task -- see open_questions.

acceptance_criteria.text: Service.StartRun calls the existing RunContext(reqCtx, budget) helper (context.WithoutCancel + WithTimeout) to build the run's execution context, only after its synchronous validation step, never passing reqCtx itself past that point.

A test cancels the context passed into StartRun immediately after StartRun returns and asserts the run still reaches a hub run.started/stage.completed sequence rather than run.cancelled with the caller's cancellation as cause.
grep for `go func` / bare `go ` across internal/pipeline/*.go finds none outside shared/concurrency; the only goroutine start for run execution is Supervisor.Go.
A test whose fake LLM panics on Complete() results in the run's status flipping to failed and a run.failed event reaching a hub subscriber, with the test process itself not crashing.

A hub subscriber attached before StartRun is called receives, over the live channel, run.started then stage.completed{analytic} (success path) or run.started then run.failed (LLM error path) or run.started then run.cancelled (context already done before analytic runs) -- published even with zero subscribers attached (verified by publishing first, subscribing after, and replaying).
A test subscribes to the hub only after the run has already completed publishing and confirms it receives the full event sequence via the replay slice, not the live channel.

A test constructs a Service with MaxConcurrentRuns=1, starts two runs back-to-back while the first is still in flight (LLM gated by a channel), and asserts the second run is admitted (RunState found, status pending) but never reaches running/failed before the first's semaphore slot is released.
`go test -race ./internal/pipeline/... ./internal/shared/concurrency/...` exits 0 with no race warnings.

A supervisor_test.go test starts several long-running fn's via Supervisor.Go, calls Shutdown with a short deadline, and asserts every fn observed its context cancelled and Shutdown returned before or at the deadline.

open_questions: SCOPE DEVIATION (flagging per 02-working.md §7, not silently deciding): the 011 prompt's acceptance criterion g5 and its orchestrator.Run pseudocode assume a `stages.Registry()` / `stage.Handler.Execute()` loop driving all 7 stages to a `run.completed` event. That infrastructure (registry.go, stages/research.go, validation.go, questioning.go, research_scoped.go, result.go) does not exist yet and is explicitly 03-backend-folder-architecture.md §9 build-order STEP 8 ("remaining 5 stages via the registry"), three steps after this one (step 5). Building it now would be a large, out-of-spec expansion (real multi-stage business logic, most of it LLM-shaped) that contradicts both this task's own §7 out-of-scope list ("any change to the 7-stage sequence itself") and task 009's already-established scope (analytic-only, stubbed LLM). Resolution taken: the Orchestrator drives exactly the sequence Service.StartRun already implemented pre-011 (scope_anchor -> analytic, stub LLM call, advance to research) and publishes events for only what actually executes: run.started, stage.completed{analytic}, run.failed, or run.cancelled. No run.completed is published, because the run's Status genuinely never reaches Done with only one of seven stages wired -- publishing it would be a false signal to any future SSE consumer. task.json g5 is written to match this scoped reality rather than the prompt's literal text. Whoever picks up build-order step 8 should extend Orchestrator.Run (or replace it with a registry-driven loop) rather than this task inventing that structure speculatively.

Abandonment policy (011 prompt §5, architecture doc §10 item 5): MaxRunDuration is set to a literal 15 minutes in platform/config (matching the architecture doc's own worked example figure) as the mechanism's default, but what happens when a run actually hits that budget -- hard-fail vs. best-effort-finish-current-stage vs. checkpoint-and-resume -- is explicitly called out in both the architecture doc and the 011 prompt as a product decision for the pilot team, not something this task decides. This task implements only the mechanism: the run context has a hard timeout and ctx.Done() during analytic execution is treated as a cancellation (run.cancelled), which is the conservative/safe default until the team picks otherwise.

Shutdown disposition (011 prompt §5, architecture doc §7.10): of the two options listed (mark unfinished runs `cancelled`, or leave them `running` for lease-based reclaim per §7.6), this task picks marking them cancelled implicitly -- Supervisor.Shutdown cancels every tracked run's context, and the orchestrator's own ctx.Done() handling then calls Run.Cancel(). No stage-ownership lease (§7.6, lease.go) exists yet to support the reclaim alternative, so cancellation is the only implementable option today, not a considered trade-off between two equally available ones. This should be revisited once §7.6's lease mechanism exists.

cmd/gateway/main.go is listed as a 'touches' file in the 011 prompt's header, but this task does NOT wire Service/Supervisor/Hub into it: there is still no concrete internal/llm implementation (only the LLM interface in deps.go; the real provider is build-order step 6, after this task and after task 012's HTTP contract), and internal/httpapi.NewRouter does not yet accept pipeline dependencies -- that DI change is task 012's own explicitly stated scope ('Current NewRouter may only accept config and database pool. This task needs the router to access the pipeline service and hub.'). Constructing a Service in main.go today with no LLM to give it and no router path to reach it would be inert scaffolding wired to nothing, which both 02-working.md's incremental-scope rule and general YAGNI argue against. Flagging rather than silently adding dead wiring or silently ignoring the prompt's file list.
risks: Rewriting service_test.go's synchronous assertions (StartRun returning the LLM error directly, RunState immediately reflecting the final result) into async ones introduces a real risk of flaky/racy tests if synchronization relies on sleeps; mitigated by synchronizing exclusively through hub subscriptions (blocking channel receives with a timeout), matching the pattern already used in hub_test.go, never a bare time.Sleep-then-assert.

Supervisor.Go's design point (derive its own cancelable child context internally, track the cancel func, so Shutdown can signal it) is an inference, not literal from the 011 prompt's pseudocode -- the prompt's `Go(ctx context.Context, fn func(context.Context))` signature has no way to hand Supervisor a cancel func directly, yet §3.2 also says Shutdown signals tracked runs 'via each entry's stored cancel func.' The only way to reconcile both without changing the public Go signature is for Supervisor to wrap the incoming ctx in its own context.WithCancel internally. Documented here so a reviewer can see this was a deliberate reading, not an oversight.

MaxConcurrentRuns semaphore's 'admitted as pending, no goroutine started' path (g7) has no mechanism in this task to later start that queued run when a slot frees -- there is no queue-drain worker. This matches §7.7's own text ('queue the run, return 202, and surface queue position through the hub') for the admission response itself, but a queued run today stays pending forever unless a future task adds a drain/retry mechanism. Flagged as a known gap, not silently pretended to be complete.

Removing/replacing NewService's two-argument signature (llm, clock) with additional required deps (hub, supervisor, maxConcurrentRuns, maxRunBudget) is a breaking change to every existing caller (service_test.go is the only in-repo caller today, since main.go doesn't construct one) -- confirmed safe to change since no production code depends on the old signature yet.
